title: Malediction Demo (2D Turn Based RPG)
author: falcon23456948
selftext: Hey guys, this is a game demo I have been working on in codex. Please let me know any advice on what to add/change that would make you play the game if you are even interested at all. It is still a work in progress. Any feedback is appreciated!

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Okay. So. 

This looks and sounds incredibly bad.

A thing I would note is that for an RPG in particular, you do not need a whole bunch of animations. Over-animating things can actually be detrimental. As an example, you just don't need a complex collapsing animation for enemies - it will be monotonous to watch even if it's good (which these are not).

Turn based RPGs also need a sense of decision making. A menu full of attacks with no apparent scheme for making those attacks matter in different ways is not an RPG, it is just pantomiming as one.

The still image sequences with text and narration look horrendous and sound completely awful. Sorry. And what is the point of them? There should be a good reason in a game to stop play and show the player something like text against a background image... and I don't see any reason to do that here. You could deliver exactly the same text and narration during play.

The menus themselves, even without playing it, look like a navigational nightmare. Why on Earth does choosing 'Fists' then branch into like a million different choices? It wasn't enough that the player had a million context-free choice before that; they must navigate a maze of esoteric options before choosing one to attack the basic starter enemy with? 

Like, I look at that thing holistically, and all I can think is, 'there isn't any design here. there isn't a game here'. 

It's a collection of things that maybe could be worked into a game, eventually, but there's nothing that you showed that looks like something a person could reasonably play with.

comments.author: phantomimp
comments.body:
Honestly, visually it looks pretty rough. Your character's movement animations make it look like he's constantly tripping over his own feet, and the directional movement is all over the place. The audio is in bad shape too.

Everyone and their mother is making AI games right now. To be commercially successful, a game needs to be truly unique, visually stunning, or fill a niche nobody else touches. Right now, I just don't see any of that in your demo.
